County board adopts data center moratorium

The county board of supervisors voted on Friday evening to adopt a twelve month moratorium on new applications for large data center projects, after three public hearings that drew hundreds of residents to the county administration building.

Supervisors said the pause would give planning staff time to draft standards for noise, water use, setbacks and backup generators. Several residents told the board that existing zoning rules were written long before hyperscale campuses were proposed in the area and do not address the scale of the buildings.

The moratorium applies to new rezoning and special exception applications. Projects that already hold approved site plans are not affected, according to the county attorney, who said the ordinance was modeled on measures adopted by neighboring jurisdictions earlier in the year.

The planning commission is expected to hold its first work session on the new standards next month, and the board said it would review progress at its regular meeting in the summer.
